name: Toyota Yaris
engine: 1.5L Skyactiv-G I4 (Mazda-built, 106 hp) on the 2016–2020 Mazda2-based US cars — earlier US Yaris used Toyota's own 1.5L (2NZ/1NR/2NR, ~106 hp)
transmission: 6-speed manual or 6-speed automatic (Mazda2-based cars) · earlier cars used a 5-speed manual or 4-speed automatic
reliability: 8/10 — the Yaris is a simple, cheap-to-run subcompact with a well-earned dependable reputation, and it is genuinely inexpensive to own. Note the twist for US buyers: the 2016–2020 Yaris sedan (and 2019–2020 hatchback) is actually a rebadged Mazda2, built by Mazda with Mazda's 1.5L Skyactiv engine and a proper 6-speed automatic — a good thing, as it drives better than the old car. Earlier US Yaris models were Toyota-built. Either way it is basic, durable transportation; Toyota discontinued it in the US after 2020.
cost_to_own: Insurance: Low · Maintenance ~$350/yr (about as cheap as cars get) · Excellent fuel economy · Resale is modest in absolute dollars but the running costs are the lowest around
popular_mods: Quality all-season or winter tires — the highest-value upgrade on any light economy car
All-weather floor liners and simple interior touches
A better head unit / speakers on base cars that came sparsely equipped
For the Mazda2-based cars, the small enthusiast scene borrows lightly from the Mazda2 parts bin
Honest take: the Yaris is about minimal running costs, not performance — spend on tires and basic upkeep and enjoy how cheap it is to own

generations.XP130 (2012–2018 US hatchback): The Toyota-built Yaris hatchback — 1.5L, 5-speed manual or 4-speed automatic. Basic and durable, if dated in tech and refinement.
generations.Mazda2-based sedan (2016–2020 US): Sold first as the Scion iA, then the Yaris iA, then simply the Yaris sedan — actually a rebadged Mazda2 with Mazda's 1.5L Skyactiv engine and a 6-speed automatic. Better to drive than the Toyota-built car.
generations.Mazda2-based hatchback (2019–2020 US): The hatchback also switched to the Mazda2 underneath for its final two years. Toyota then dropped the Yaris from the US lineup after 2020.

common_issues: Modest power and a basic feel — it is an economy car and does not hide it
Road and wind noise on the highway, as with any light subcompact
Sparse equipment on base trims (especially the older Toyota-built cars)
US availability ended after 2020, so parts/service are straightforward but it is an older platform now
Confirm any open recalls (including the older Takata airbag campaigns on early cars) are closed by VIN
maintenance_tips: Keep up with the specified synthetic oil — these engines ask for very little
On the Mazda2-based cars, service the 6-speed automatic fluid on schedule for a long life
Check the Takata airbag and any open recalls by VIN on older examples — free and important
Otherwise it is cabin filters, brake fluid, and tires; parts are cheap and everywhere
The manual's clutch is light and long-lived; just keep the hydraulic fluid fresh
